scenes.heading: Property and Lucene Indexes
scenes.narration: Oak & Operations. Property and Lucene Indexes. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: Where are indexes configured, and what node type must an index definition use?
scenes.heading: Indexes are configured as nodes under oak:index, and the node type must be oak:QueryIndexDefinition
scenes.body: Section 3 says indexes are configured as nodes under oak:index, using node type oak:QueryIndexDefinition.

scenes.question: What kind of queries does the Property Index suit, and which two properties define it?
scenes.heading: It suits property constraints that are not full-text, and it uses type set to property with propertyNames listing the properties
scenes.body: Section 3 says the Property Index suits property constraints that are not full-text and uses type property with propertyNames.

scenes.question: What do the unique flag, declaringNodeTypes, and reindex=true do on a Property Index?
scenes.heading: The unique flag adds a uniqueness constraint, declaringNodeTypes restricts the index to a node type, and reindex=true triggers a full reindex
scenes.body: Section 3 defines these directly: unique adds a uniqueness constraint, declaringNodeTypes restricts the node type, and reindex=true triggers a full reindex.

scenes.question: What does the speech say about the Ordered index?
scenes.heading: The Ordered index is deprecated and should be replaced with a Lucene Property Index

scenes.question: Which two main settings does the Lucene full-text index use, and what delay tradeoff does the speech mention?
scenes.heading: It uses type lucene and async set to async, so some full-text results can be unavailable briefly after a change

scenes.question: What does the speech say happens when a full-text index is configured, and what if none is configured?
scenes.heading: If a full-text index is configured, all queries with a full-text condition use it; if none is configured, full-text conditions do not work as expected
scenes.body: Section 3 says a configured full-text index is used for all queries with a full-text condition, and without one those conditions do not work as expected.

scenes.question: How do you configure Lucene to index non-full-text property constraints, and what consistency note comes with it?
scenes.heading: Set fulltextEnabled to false and list the properties in includePropertyNames; a Lucene Property Index is always async, so results may lag behind the latest state
scenes.body: Section 3 says Lucene can index non-full-text property constraints with fulltextEnabled=false and includePropertyNames, but it remains async.
